newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MINISTER ACCUSES ADVERTISERS OF RACISM.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MINISTER ACCUSES ADVERTISERS OF RACISM.

text.p: A Zimbabwean cabinet minister has accused local advertising and public relations organisations of practising institutionalised racism.

Information, Posts and Telecommunications Minister Joyce Mujuru said at a closed door meeting with industry executives on Monday night that 16 years after Zimbabwe gained black majority rule, the sector was still controlled by minority whites.

"I am aware that relationships in your business are largely based on the old school-tie network, a practice that has served you well for many years...but I don't have to remind you that this translates into one racial group keeping out other racial groups," she was quoted as saying by the state news agency ZIANA.
Industry officials were not immediately available for comment, and ZIANA did not say how the executives responded at the meeting.

"As government continues to open up the economy and consumers flex their muscles, you, the advertising agencies and related industries, need to recognise and reflect these changes and the demographic reality in Zimbabwe.

"How many black Zimbabweans do your companies employ and how many are in key senior positions?," she asked, accusing the industry of using rules and regulations aimed at creating monopolies and cartels.
Zimbabwean whites make up less than one percent of the country's 10.5 million population and the government has regularly accused them of racism despite their stout denials.
Mujuru also asked the advertising and public relations industry to help her government promote Zimbabwe's investment profile abroad.
